translation_note: World English Bible (Public Domain). Preserves 'Yahweh' in Old Testament passages where the divine name (YHWH) appears in Hebrew — 9 of the 39 sample entries use it. See translation_notes for the affected references and the choice to keep them faithful to WEB rather than substituting 'the LORD'.

translation_notes.rationale: If you prefer the traditional 'the LORD' rendering for user-facing text, a global search-replace of 'Yahweh' → 'the LORD' on the key_verse.text field is safe and legally valid (WEB is public domain and may be modified). The bible.com deep-link continues to open the user's chosen translation regardless of stored key_verse text.

purpose: Reviewable sample of passage boundaries, summaries, and key verses for the Canonical Scripture Journey. Once approved (or edited), these entries drop directly into the 1,000-day master plan at canonical-web-v1.json with no reformatting.

schema.day: integer position in the master plan (populated for the first 14; null for the topical samples until they're placed on their calendar day)
schema.passages: array of one or more passage ranges — a day is usually one range, but occasionally two paired ranges when a natural section spans a chapter boundary
schema.key_verse: the single verse that best summarizes the reading; stored as metadata, never computed at runtime
schema.passage_summary: one to two sentences that give the model (and eventually the user) the context of the whole reading, biblically descriptive, neutral in interpretation

key_verse.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.

first_14_days.passage_summary: In the opening days of creation God speaks light, sky, land, sea, plants, luminaries, sea creatures, and birds into being, calling each good.

key_verse.text: God created man in his own image. In God's image he created him; male and female he created them.

first_14_days.passage_summary: God creates humanity in his own image, male and female, gives dominion over creation, and rests on the seventh day, blessing it and setting it apart.

key_verse.text: Yahweh God said, 'It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make him a helper comparable to him.'

first_14_days.passage_summary: God plants a garden in Eden, forms the man from the dust, gives him work and a command, and fashions a woman from his side — the first marriage.

key_verse.text: I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.

first_14_days.passage_summary: The serpent tempts the woman, the man eats, and both are exposed. God pronounces judgment on serpent, woman, and man, and speaks a first promise of a coming offspring who will crush the serpent.

key_verse.text: If you do well, won't it be lifted up? If you don't do well, sin crouches at the door. Its desire is for you, but you are to rule over it.

first_14_days.passage_summary: Cain kills Abel and is sent east of Eden; his line grows in the city and in the arts, while through Seth another line begins to call on the name of Yahweh.

key_verse.text: But Noah found favor in Yahweh's eyes.

first_14_days.passage_summary: The genealogy runs from Adam through Enoch, who walked with God, to Noah. As human wickedness fills the earth and grieves God's heart, Noah finds favor in Yahweh's eyes.

key_verse.text: Thus Noah did. According to all that God commanded him, so he did.

first_14_days.passage_summary: God tells Noah to build an ark to survive the coming flood. Noah obeys in every detail, and the waters rise until they cover the highest mountains.

key_verse.text: I set my rainbow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth.

first_14_days.passage_summary: God remembers Noah, the waters recede, and Noah offers worship on dry land. God blesses Noah and his sons and establishes a covenant with all creation, marked by the rainbow.

key_verse.text: They said, 'Come, let's build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top reaches to the sky, and let's make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered abroad on the surface of the whole earth.'

first_14_days.passage_summary: The nations spread from Noah's sons. When humanity gathers at Shinar to build a city and a tower to make a name for itself, God confuses their language and scatters them across the earth.

key_verse.text: I will make of you a great nation. I will bless you and make your name great. You will be a blessing. I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse him who treats you with contempt. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you.

first_14_days.passage_summary: The genealogy narrows from Shem to Abram. God calls Abram to leave country, kindred, and father's house for a land he does not know, promising blessing on him and, through him, on all the families of the earth.

key_verse.text: Blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand.

first_14_days.passage_summary: Abram and Lot separate as their households grow. When Lot is captured in a war of kings, Abram rescues him, and Melchizedek — priest of God Most High — meets Abram with bread, wine, and blessing.

key_verse.text: He believed in Yahweh, who credited it to him for righteousness.

first_14_days.passage_summary: In a vision, God renews the promise of countless offspring and a land. Abram believes God, and his faith is counted as righteousness; the covenant is sealed with a torch passing between the pieces of a sacrifice.

key_verse.text: I am God Almighty. Walk before me and be blameless.

first_14_days.passage_summary: Sarai gives Hagar to Abram; Ishmael is born, and God meets Hagar in the wilderness. Years later God renames Abram Abraham and Sarai Sarah, promises Isaac within the year, and gives circumcision as the sign of the covenant.

key_verse.text: Is anything too hard for Yahweh? At the set time I will return to you, when the season comes around, and Sarah will have a son.

first_14_days.passage_summary: Three visitors promise Sarah a son within the year. Abraham intercedes for Sodom, and when judgment comes on Sodom and Gomorrah, Lot is rescued while his wife looks back.

key_verse.text: but his delight is in Yahweh's law. On his law he meditates day and night.

psalms_sample.passage_summary: The psalter opens by contrasting two paths: the righteous who delight in God's law and flourish like a tree by streams, and the wicked whose way blows away like chaff.

key_verse.text: Yahweh is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing.

psalms_sample.passage_summary: David sings of the Lord as shepherd who provides, restores, and walks with him through the darkest valley, with goodness and mercy following him all his days.

key_verse.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.

psalms_sample.passage_summary: After his sin with Bathsheba, David turns to God with grief and asks for cleansing, a right spirit, and the joy of salvation restored; God delights in a broken and contrite heart.

key_verse.text: He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty. I will say of Yahweh, 'He is my refuge and my fortress; my God, in whom I trust.'

psalms_sample.passage_summary: A psalm of refuge: those who dwell in the secret place of the Most High rest in the shadow of the Almighty, promised protection, deliverance, and the presence of God.

key_verse.text: I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful. My soul knows that very well.

psalms_sample.passage_summary: David marvels that God knows him fully — his thoughts, his going out and coming in, his frame formed in the womb — and invites God to search him and lead him in the everlasting way.

key_verse.text: Trust in Yahweh with all your heart, and don't lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.

proverbs_sample.passage_summary: A father urges his son to trust the Lord with all his heart, honor him with his substance, and accept his discipline — for the Lord disciplines those he loves as a father does the son he delights in.

key_verse.text: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.

proverbs_sample.passage_summary: A father calls his son to attend to wisdom's words and keep his heart with all diligence, since life flows from it — and to keep his eyes, mouth, and feet aligned with that watchful heart.

key_verse.text: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.

proverbs_sample.passage_summary: A collection of proverbs on the power of speech, the fear of the Lord, and the state of the heart — the tongue of the wise commends knowledge and a joyful heart makes the face cheerful.

key_verse.text: Commit your deeds to Yahweh, and your plans shall succeed.

proverbs_sample.passage_summary: The plans of the heart belong to a person, but the answer of the tongue is from the Lord. Those who commit their work to him and walk in humility find their steps established.

key_verse.text: Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.

proverbs_sample.passage_summary: A good name is worth more than great riches. The wise train their children, guard against pride, and remember that the rich and poor share one Maker.

key_verse.text: I heard the Lord's voice, saying, 'Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?' Then I said, 'Here I am. Send me!'

prophetic_sample.passage_summary: Isaiah sees the Lord high and lifted up while seraphim cry 'Holy, holy, holy.' Undone by his uncleanness, Isaiah is cleansed by a burning coal, then answers God's call to go.

key_verse.text: but those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.

prophetic_sample.passage_summary: Comfort is spoken to a weary people: every valley raised, every mountain leveled, and the glory of the Lord revealed. The everlasting God does not grow weary, and those who wait on him find their strength renewed.

key_verse.text: But he was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought our peace was on him; and by his wounds we are healed.

prophetic_sample.passage_summary: The prophet describes a servant despised and rejected, pierced for the transgressions of others and crushed for their iniquities — bearing the sins of many and interceding for the guilty.

key_verse.text: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, says Yahweh, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.

prophetic_sample.passage_summary: Jeremiah writes to the exiles in Babylon: build houses, plant gardens, seek the peace of the city. God has not forgotten them — his plans are for their good, and he will bring them home when they call to him.

key_verse.text: I will also give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you. I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh.

prophetic_sample.passage_summary: For the sake of his own name, God promises to gather his scattered people, cleanse them, and give them a new heart and a new spirit — his own Spirit within them, moving them to walk in his ways.

key_verse.text: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.

gospel_sample.passage_summary: On the mountain, Jesus opens his teaching by pronouncing blessing on the poor in spirit, those who mourn, the meek, the pure in heart, and the peacemakers, then calls his followers to be salt of the earth and light of the world.

key_verse.text: Pray like this: 'Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.'

gospel_sample.passage_summary: Jesus warns against praying for show or for words' sake, and gives his disciples a pattern to follow — a prayer that honors the Father's name, seeks his kingdom, asks for daily bread, and forgives as it has been forgiven.

key_verse.text: He arose, and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

gospel_sample.passage_summary: A younger son squanders his inheritance and returns home in ruin. Before he can finish his confession, the father runs to embrace him — while the elder brother's cold resentment shows how grace troubles the self-righteous.

key_verse.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

gospel_sample.passage_summary: Nicodemus comes to Jesus by night. Jesus tells him no one can see the kingdom without being born of water and Spirit — for God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes might have eternal life.

key_verse.text: I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.

gospel_sample.passage_summary: Jesus is the true vine and the Father is the gardener. Apart from him, branches wither; abiding in him and in his love, they bear much fruit — the mark of true disciples.

key_verse.text: There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus, who don't walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.

epistle_sample.passage_summary: What the law could not do because of the flesh, God did through his Son. For those in Christ Jesus there is no condemnation — the same Spirit who raised Jesus lives in believers, making them children and heirs of God.

key_verse.text: Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service.

epistle_sample.passage_summary: In view of God's mercies, Paul urges believers to present themselves as living sacrifices — not conformed to this age but transformed by the renewing of their minds, using their gifts humbly and overcoming evil with good.

key_verse.text: But now faith, hope, and love remain—these three. The greatest of these is love.

epistle_sample.passage_summary: Without love, every gift is empty noise. Love is patient and kind, keeps no record of wrongs, and endures all things. Faith and hope will remain, but love is the greatest.

key_verse.text: for by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, that no one would boast.

epistle_sample.passage_summary: Once dead in trespasses, believers have been made alive with Christ and raised with him — saved by grace through faith, not by works, but created in Christ for good works God prepared beforehand.

key_verse.text: In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.

epistle_sample.passage_summary: Paul urges the Philippians to rejoice always, be anxious for nothing, and bring every request to God with thanksgiving — and God's peace, beyond understanding, will guard their hearts. He has learned contentment through Christ who strengthens him.
